question.en: Why do AI Engineer postings require Docker and at least one cloud platform even for application-layer roles?

answer.en: 86.8% of AI-First postings require skills beyond GenAI, and the most common pairing is GenAI plus ops (Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD) at 70.6% (AI Engineering Field Guide). AWS leads the clouds with 40.3% of postings, ahead of Azure 29.6% and GCP 27.4%. The reason is the job itself: the work is running and maintaining a service in production against the company data. Even application-layer roles own deployment, basic monitoring and environment parity, so a portfolio that only ships notebooks does not demonstrate the role.

question.en: What does a minimal production-ready service around an LLM call look like, and which tests does it need?

answer.en: A thin FastAPI (or Node) service with two endpoints: one that wraps the model call (structured output, timeout, retry with backoff) and one health or readiness check. Secrets come from the environment, never from the repository. Behavioural tests in Pytest cover the output schema, the error paths (model timeout, invalid input) and token or cost accounting if it is exposed. A Dockerfile pins the runtime so the service behaves the same locally and on the cloud. Keep it small on purpose: the gate is a working, tested, deployed service, not a framework showcase.

question.en: SQL is requested less in AI Engineer postings than in general tech postings. Which data skills still matter for the role?

answer.en: In Spain SQL appears in 23.3% of AI Engineer postings versus 27.8% of general tech postings, the only signal that goes down (nothiring.me). Data access does not disappear though: PostgreSQL is the default database in the field guide stack list, vector databases appear in about 1,647 of 6,964 postings, and grounding a model in company data means modelling that data for retrieval. The useful skill is schema design plus knowing when to answer from structured data with a query instead of stuffing the prompt.

question.en: Python shows up in most AI Engineer postings. What Python depth do interviewers actually probe beyond writing scripts?

answer.en: Python appears in about 70.8% of the 6,964 analyzed postings (AI Engineering Field Guide) and in 78.8% of AI Engineer postings in Spain (nothiring.me), because most AI libraries and SDKs ship Python first. Interviewers probe beyond scripting: type hints and dataclasses for structured data, virtual environments and packaging, Pytest-style behavioural tests, async patterns and GIL awareness (concurrency versus parallelism), and clean HTTP clients around model APIs. The bar is not ML research code; it is reading and modifying a real Python service without mentally translating it to JavaScript.

question.en: What separates intermediate SQL from basic SQL in production work?

answer.en: Basics read rows; intermediate SQL shapes and defends them. Window functions compute rankings, running totals and period deltas without self-joins — ROW_NUMBER, LAG/LEAD over (PARTITION BY ... ORDER BY ...) — and they run after WHERE, so filter ranked rows in a subquery. EXPLAIN ANALYZE shows the plan tree with real numbers beside the estimates: a sequential scan on a big table, a bad join order, or a function wrapped around an indexed column explains most slow queries, and Rows Removed by Filter shows the waste. Then the correctness traps interviews love: NULLs make NOT IN match nothing and drop rows from aggregates, implicit casts defeat indexes, and GROUP BY must cover the select list. Being able to read a plan and kill the self-join is the bar.
